This fractography reference presents microstructural data across a wide range of engineering alloys. The following tabulated observations summarise phase identification, fracture-mode relations, and metallographic conditions extracted from the handbook.

\begin{longtable}{|p{0.20\linewidth}|p{0.20\linewidth}|p{0.45\linewidth}|}
\hline
\textbf{Material} & \textbf{Condition / Treatment} & \textbf{Microstructural Features} \\
\hline\hline
\endfirsthead
\hline
\textbf{Material} & \textbf{Condition / Treatment} & \textbf{Microstructural Features} \\
\hline\hline
\endhead
AISI 4140 steel & Step-cool

The following table summarises the heat treatment data extracted from the fractography reference atlas. The data are presented as background context for fractographic interpretation rather than as a controlled experimental matrix. The standard hint requested was for ``platinum properties''; however, no platinum or platinum-group metal data appear in the supplied source text. Materials covered include alloy steels (AISI 1045, ASTM A508 class II), stainless steels (25Cr-12Ni cast, type 312), malleable irons (ferritic, pearlitic), iron-aluminium alloys, Ti-6Al-4V, Ti-1.8Mn, Fe-3.9Ni, Fe-12Ni-0.5T

{
  "notes": [
    "Document 1_12 - Fractography.pdf is Volume 12 of the ASM Handbook (1987) on Fractography \u2014 a general reference/textbook, NOT a Material Test Report (MTR), EN 10204 inspection certificate, foundry/forging report, NACE test report, weld procedure record, NDT certificate, or dimensional/weight certificate. Therefore, conventional metallurgical certificate data (heat number, ladle/product analysis, mechanical test results, hardness, NDT, sour-service, etc.) is NOT present.",
    "No specific platinum properties data found in the document despite the 'platinum properties' standard hint. The handbook is a general fractography reference covering fracture modes, history of fractography, effect of environment, and discontinuities leading to fracture. Platinum is not a subject of detailed coverage in the provided pages.",
    "Section focus 'surface_quality' \u2014 relevant surface-quality information extracted from the document: preparation/preservation of fracture specimens, photography of fracture surfaces, visual examination and light microscopy of surfaces, corrosion products obscuring fracture surface detail, oxide buildup at elevated temperature, and surface fracture features (fatigue striations, dimples, cleavage facets, river patterns, tire tracks, tongues, flutes, knobbly structure, etc.).",
    "Surface fracture features documented (descriptive, not as measured values): dimple rupture (equiaxed/elongated/oval dimples), cleavage (river patterns, feather markings, chevron/herringbone patterns, tongues, Wallner lines), fatigue (Stage I, II, III; striations, tire tracks, plateaus), decohesive rupture (intergranular facets, creep cavities/wedge cracks), quasi-cleavage, flutes, tearing topography surface (TTS), knobbly structure from adiabatic shear bands, mud-crack pattern of corrosion products.",
    "Corrosion-product and oxide surface effects noted: corrosion products can appear as powdery residue, amorphous films, or crystalline deposits; corrosion products may exhibit cleavage fracture and secondary cracking; removing corrosion products will NOT restore a fracture to its original condition; progressive oxide obscuration demonstrated on Ti-6Al-2Sn-4Zr-6Mo at 700 \u00b0C (1290 \u00b0F) in air (3, 10, 30 min exposures); severe oxidation at 800 \u00b0C (1470 \u00b0F)/15 min in air on Ti-6Al-6V-2Sn made fracture mode unidentifiable; 5 min at 700 \u00b0C (1290 \u00b0F) air exposure on 300M steel (2028 MPa / 294 ksi UTS) covered entire fracture surface with oxide.",
    "Cleaning of fracture surfaces referenced: cleaning in acetone in an ultrasonic cleaner revealed striations and pitting on austenitic stainless steel hip implant (Brooks & Choudhury); acid-cleaning residues on Nb-106 alloy contributed to SCC failure (Kashar).",
    "Marking/identification: fracture surfaces from failed service components cited include AISI 5160 wire springs (seam origin), 300M high-strength steel stud (laps from thread rolling), AISI 4340 steel parts (tensile strength 1790\u20131930 MPa / 260\u2013280 ksi, pre-existing SCC crack), AISI 9310 case-hardened steel forging (firebrick inclusion), A357-T6 cast Al air-turbine blade (inclusion), AISI 4340 steel forging (1380\u20131520 MPa / 200\u2013220 ksi, stringers, overload during straightening), 7075-T6 spot weld (porosity).",
    "Fracture mode \u2192 environment \u2192 surface appearance qualitative findings (representative): hydrogen gas on steels increases Stage II crack growth rate up to 10\u00d7 and promotes intergranular decohesion/cleavage/quasi-cleavage on fracture surface; 1-atm hydrogen on Ti-6Al-4V produced transgranular fracture (705 \u00b0C/2 h AC) vs. intergranular decohesion along \u03b1-\u03b2 boundaries (955 \u00b0C/40 min) vs. terraced prior-\u03b2 grain boundary fracture (1040 \u00b0C/40 min); sulfur-containing atmospheres on Inconel 718 at 650 \u00b0C (1200 \u00b0F) produced thick adherent scales obscuring fracture detail; H2S more aggressive than SO2 on Incoloy 800 at 316\u2013650 \u00b0C; aqueous 3% NaCl on low-alloy steel produced coarser river patterns confined to single grains vs. air fracture; cryogenic (-196 \u00b0C / -320 \u00b0F) on 1100-Al and 99.99% Al reduced crack growth rate by factor 20\u201380 (fracture surfaces not examined per source)."
  ]
}
